text.p: Nepal's trade deficit for the first eleven months of the 1996/97 fiscal surged to 67.08 billion rupees, 31.9 percent more than 50.87 billion rupees in the same period of 1995/96, the central bank said on Thursday.
Nepal's fiscal year starts on July 16.
Exports rose to 20.80 billion rupees from 18.38 billion rupees in 1995/96, while imports rose to 87.88 billion rupees compared to 69.26 billion rupees the previous year, the Nepal Rastra Bank said.
The central bank said the kingdom's total budget in 1996/97 totalled 51.1 billion rupees, up from 46.54 billion rupees in 1995/96.
Bank officials said exports of hand-knotted woollen carpets increased to 8.2 billion rupees from 7.5 billion and readymade garments to 5.4 billion rupees from 5.0 billion.
Carpets and readymade garments are the two principal exports of Nepal, one of the world's 10 poorest countries.
Refusal by the Western buyers to accept Nepali carpets that use child labour and inferior chemicals has hit carpet exports and forced the government to take corrective measures.
Authorities began giving child labour-free tags to Nepali rugs since October last year but the scheme covers only 25 percent of the producers.
Last year, the government banned the import of azo dye, a poor quality colouring chemical, to redress the concerns of the Western buyers of Nepali rugs.
